[SYSTEM]
You are a senior absolute oral bioavailability F-threshold reasoning model. Integrate evidence direction and transferability without converting uncertainty into a negative outcome. 

L6 adds hepatic-clearance and metabolic-stability experiments. Use them as mechanistic evidence for systemic presystemic loss while preserving species, assay system, and measurement direction; they are not direct oral- bioavailability results or extra gold votes.

This is progressive assay-transfer reasoning. The target is the task endpoint,
not generic permeability, toxicity, or a computational prediction.

Record cards expose source-native values under their original column names.
Missing source values are omitted; do not assume a hidden canonicalized value.


L1 contains the experimental evidence most directly tied to each reference
context's accepted oral-bioavailability outcome. Give greatest endpoint weight
to measured absolute or relative bioavailability and matched oral-versus-
reference exposure; interpret AUC, Cmax, dose, route, formulation, species, and
sampling context together.

L2 adds related experimental records for the same molecule and exact condition.
Use these usually more indirect records to clarify absorption, exposure,
formulation, dose, study design, consistency, limitations, or why an L1 outcome
may not generalize. Permeability, solubility, or mechanism alone is not a direct
oral-bioavailability outcome.


First determine what every measurement says about its reference molecule. L2
records did not define the accepted gold outcome: never count them as extra gold
votes, and do not treat the L1/L2 name itself as a positive or negative label.

Treat transfer_likelihood as one relevance signal for whether a reference
parent-condition context may apply to the query. It is not a positive-class
probability, an experimental result, or a substitute for reasoning about the
visible structure, endpoint, assay, species, formulation, exposure, and
condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from
all visible context. Do not invent a numeric similarity judgment or assume that
a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

Use general medicinal-chemistry knowledge to interpret structures, but ground
every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

claims.claim: Directly transferable nucleoside-analog contexts show measured oral F above 20%: zalcitabine ~80% in fasted patients (C29), didanosine fasting F 0.22–0.28 (C08, C14), zidovudine F 0.61±0.22 in cirrhosis (C10), didanosine 42% (C45), children F 0.27±0.13 (C68), and zalcitabine 30% in fasted mice (C62).

The close polar ribonucleoside ribavirin is highly soluble across physiological pH (C141, C133, C138) and shows substantial oral exposure (AUC0-12 3325.83 ng·h/mL, Tmax 1.61 h; C92, C82); lamivudine 300 mg also shows substantial oral exposure (AUC0-inf 13.2 µg·h/mL, Cmax 3.3 µg/mL; C100, C119). This supports that polar ribonucleosides can achieve F≥20% despite low passive permeability.

L5 provides mechanistic support for transporter-mediated intestinal uptake of polar nucleosides: NHC is a substrate of CNT1/2/3/ENT2 (C216), gemcitabine entry is transporter-dependent (C205), lamivudine has measurable Caco-2 uptake permeability (C197), didanosine shows L→B intestinal perfusion 1.4×10^-6 cm/s (C200), F-ddI shows L→B 3.3×10^-6 cm/s (C191), and a nucleoside sulfamate showed no efflux (C231).

L6 shows that nucleoside analogs can have low hepatic metabolic clearance: GS-441524 is not a substrate of major CYP isoforms (C264, C276), zidovudine has a low predicted hepatic clearance of 1.7 ml/min/kg from HLM scaling (C236, C274), and EdUrd has a low hepatic clearance of 1.29 ml/min in isolated perfused rat liver (C279). This supports that hepatic first-pass is not an automatic barrier for this class.

The only sub-20% nucleoside F record, gemcitabine in mice (C47), is low-transferability and reflects a different metabolic liability (deamination); low passive permeability and efflux for other nucleosides (C132, C178, C172) are mechanism-only and do not affirmatively establish F<20% for AICAR.

evidence_gaps: No direct absolute oral bioavailability measurement for AICAR/acadesine is present in the supplied records.
No AICAR-specific hepatic clearance or metabolic stability data are present; L6 transfer is from other nucleosides such as GS-441524, zidovudine, and EdUrd.

No AICAR-specific permeability, transporter, efflux, or intestinal metabolism experiment is present; L4/L5 transfer is from other nucleosides such as ribavirin, lamivudine, NHC, didanosine, and gemcitabine.
Analog oral F values are variable (e.g., didanosine 22–42%, zalcitabine 29–100%), so population-level inference is uncertain.
AICAR-specific metabolism (e.g., adenosine kinase phosphorylation) is not covered by the supplied records.

No direct AICAR measurement is available, so confidence remains moderate.
